---
title: "meinequality"
subtitle: "Marginal effect inequality: summarizing the effects of a categorical predictor"
---

A nominal predictor with several categories produces a set of marginal effects
-- one contrast for every pair of categories. `meinequality` summarizes that set
in a single measure of how unequal the categories are, with a standard error, so
that the overall importance of a categorical variable can be reported, compared
across predictors, and compared across models or groups.

<!-- CHECK: definition sentence and the citation for the measure (Mize & Han).

## Installation

```stata
net install meinequality, from("https://tdmize.github.io/data/meinequality") replace
```

<!-- CHECK: install location. -->

## Basic use

```{.stata-run}
. sysuse nlsw88, clear
(NLSW, 1988 extract)

. drop if missing(union)
(368 observations deleted)

. 
. quietly logit union i.race i.collgrad c.age i.south, vce(robust)

. 
. meinequality race
Model (meineq_mod1) is:
     logit union i.race i.collgrad c.age i.south, vce(robust)

ME Inequality Estimates (N = 1878)

                         |   Estimate   Std. err.           z       P>|z| 
-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------
ME Inequality            |                                               
                    race |      0.106       0.025       4.225       0.000 

```

With no `models()` option the summary is computed for the model in memory;
with two stored models in `models()` it is computed for each and the
difference is tested, as in [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html).

## Documentation

`help meinequality` in Stata documents the syntax and options. The same
summary is available as an option of [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html),
which places it beneath the marginal effects it summarizes.
